The threat of nuclear terrorism has not gone away, and we cannot afford to be complacent. Over the past several years, working with partners around the world, we have removed or disposed of enough nuclear material to make many hundreds of weapons. We have secured vulnerable sites, strengthened international agreements, and trained thousands of experts. But the work isn’t finished. Materials remain in too many places with too little protection, and terrorists continue to seek them. That is why it is essential that we keep up the pace, that we hold each other accountable, and that we make this a priority regardless of the headlines. Security is only as strong as its weakest link. Today I’m asking each of you to ask what more you can do, and then to do it.
